### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, touching **41** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f12667f44fdf075578d9e02d33cea6d04576957a` — the merge of head `fe88538bdf92a9d482fb4677c6a8cfa501028a97` into base `3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f12667f44fdf075578d9e02d33cea6d04576957a && git checkout f12667f44fdf075578d9e02d33cea6d04576957a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda fe88538bdf92a9d482fb4677c6a8cfa501028a97 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda && git merge --no-ff fe88538bdf92a9d482fb4677c6a8cfa501028a97

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Head-sha: `c2ad15cf6d1732a16da5092c30b6f2e194f83cc3`

the one prose path, `.changeset/32351-history-rollback-by-package.md`, was read for its two declaration lines and its ADR-0087 marker only) + cited code read, not reviewed: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata.object.ts, packages/drivers (the `syncSchema` doors of driver-sql, driver-turso, driver-mongodb, driver-memory), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs, .changeset/config.json

Inputs read: card #32351 and its eight comments (claim 6814007667, seat ruling 6814172483, dev report 6815747954), the PR body, the diff of merge-base `2359ceadc` to the head (28 files, +506 −49), the three source files and the test file whole at the head, the head's check-runs. Nothing was built or run; the dev's md5 table, red/green counts, ablation and dogfood battery are the dev's readings and are not re-measured here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **FROM → TO, one-holder side: complete.** Read through `rollbackSlot`, `historyPackageAddress`, `getHistoryRecord`, `queryHistory`, `registerRollback` and the three manager doors. With one row slot and no package named, the only answer that moves is a rollback whose version is attributed to a package other than the slot's (the history row's `package_id`, else the body's stamp). Every variant of it falls under the declared wording "a version of a package that holds no row of the name": the remaining slot is another package's, or the package-less row; the attribution comes from the column or from a legacy body stamp. Reads with one slot add one `sys_metadata` read (`rowSlots`) and return the same rows: the history record mapping is unchanged and does not expose the new column. A type outside `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES` takes the old branch in every door. The dev's md5 8/8 claim agrees with this reading; it is not a second measurement.
- **FROM → TO, multi-slot side: declared, with two edges the lines do not spell.** (a) "Two row slots" includes a package's row beside the package-less row; the changeset says so, the PR body's FROM → TO does not. (b) `MetadataManager.rollback` and `diff` naming no package on a two-slot name with a version that does not exist: FROM a plain `Version N not found` error TO the 409, because `getHistoryRecord` now refuses before the row is read. Both are inside the two-holder narrowing; neither is a one-holder move.
- **Schema face.** `package_id` is `Field.text`, nullable, `maxLength: 255`, the same shape as `sys_metadata.package_id`. Driver mode: `ensureHistorySchema` calls `syncSchema`, and the SQL family adds a missing column additively (driver-sql's additive sync, driver-turso's own `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`); driver-mongodb and driver-memory have no column DDL and store the key only when a writer passes it. Engine mode leaves the sync to ObjectQL startup, which syncs the registered object. No row is rewritten; no code in the diff or in the readers I searched (CLI organization-ownership, the metadata migrations, history cleanup, the repository) rebuilds the table from a fixed column list. The dev's pin creates the table without the column on `driver-sqlite-wasm` and then reads `[1, null], [2, null], [3, A]`; other dialects rest on the shared code path, not on a pin.
- **Unique `(type, name, version)`: still right.** `nextNameVersion` numbers a by-package name over every package's row and over the history rows (#32246), and `SysMetadataRepository` numbers per `(type, name)` from the history maximum, so two packages of one name never share a version. The column does not join the key and must not: it is NULL on legacy rows.
- **Who fills the column.** `DatabaseLoader` only, at its three `createHistoryRecord` calls (`create`, `update`, `revert`), with the slot's package: the body's package, the one holder for a package-less customization (D4), the package that takes over a package-less row. NULL stays on a package-less row, on every other type, on every `SysMetadataRepository` row (the ruling), and on rows written before the column. `storedRowPackageId` reads the column first and the body stamp second, so a NULL row is never given a package it does not name: the failure mode is "no package", not a wrong package. Two residuals follow and are graded in ④ (N2, S1).
- **Refusal shape.** Both refusals are `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` built with `packageScopedRefusalMessage` (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, 409, `refusal.reason`, `callerPackageId`, `candidates`), the envelope of the other D3 doors; the tests assert `code`, `status`, `reason`, `callerPackageId` and `candidates` on the main cases. Two shapes are off (S2).
- **Generated bundles.** Each of the 11 `*.objects.generated.ts` gains the same three lines after `version`, in the field's declared position; each of the 10 non-English `*.source-hashes.generated.ts` gains one line with the same digest `cf01d56712075feb`. The English copy plus a source-hash entry is the repo's norm for an untranslated leaf: the hash file's own header defines an entry as "this leaf is still a byte copy of its source", and sibling rows (`…fields.id.label`) follow it. `en` has no hash file, which gives 11 + 10. No hand-edit is visible, and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which runs `check:i18n`) is `success` on the head.
- **Changeset claim "no first-party door reaches `DatabaseLoader` history".** Holds on the head: `getHistory`, `queryHistory`, `getHistoryRecord` and `registerRollback` have no caller outside `metadata-manager.ts` and tests under `packages/` and `apps/`.

### ② Semver level

- `fix(metadata)!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct. Nothing a metadata author can write is added, removed or changed; `sys_metadata_history` is a platform table served only through the metadata API, and `IMetadataService` in `packages/spec` is untouched (the manager's parameters widen, which the interface accepts).
- `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata` and `@objectstack/metadata-core` with the `**BREAKING**` banner: what AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 prescribes for a breaking non-protocol change. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: consistent with the lane's sibling changesets (#32347, #32198) and with the fact that nothing stored needs converting. See N4 for the wording the dev changed to clear the gate.
- **should-fix (S3, the seat's ACCEPT face):** the diff also moves `@objectstack/platform-objects` (11 shipped bundles gain a key) and the changeset does not name it. The last six commits on `main` that regenerated these bundles each carry `'@objectstack/platform-objects': patch`. The fixed group bumps the package either way and `Check Changeset` is green, so this is the changelog entry only.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no other login to name.
- File surface: inside claim 6814007667 as widened by 6814172483. The 10 source-hash companions are generator output of the same command and are declared in the dev report's deviations. No path under `packages/spec/**`, `ui/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**` or `AGENTS.md`.
- Governed surface: `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`; no published-schema or governed-rule path in the tree. The tier is owed by the narrowing declaration.
- Security: none found. The new option is a map key and an in-memory comparison; it reaches no query text, and the table's object gate (`studio.access`) is unchanged.
- Check-runs on the head at the time of writing: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (among them `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`). Still `in_progress`: `Test Core (1/8)` to `(8/8)` and `Type Check · workspace`. The all-green condition is not yet met and is the seat's to re-read.
- Overlap, named not judged. #32507 at its head `2c6503517` does not touch `database-loader.ts`; the PR body's sentence that it edits `registerRollback`'s region is stale. It edits `package-slotted-store.ts` at lines 51 and 99 (adds `flow` to `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES`), away from this PR's insertion at 441, so a textual conflict is unlikely. The risk is semantic: whichever lands second, `flow` becomes a seventh by-package type, this PR's pins iterate it automatically (seven more cases the other PR never ran, on a `{ name, label, locale }` body), `DatabaseLoader` history of flows narrows under a declaration that names six types, and the six-type list in this changeset goes stale. #32513 and #32558 widen the same set the same way. Textual risk sits elsewhere: #32548 edits `database-loader.ts` (hunks at 1251, 1716, 1990) and the tail of `metadata-manager.ts` (hunk at 4082, where this PR adds its two helpers); #32533 and #32551 edit `package-slotted-store.ts` between 371 and 532, around this PR's new `refuseSlotNotHeld`.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published contract on `main`: `IMetadataService.getHistory` / `rollback` / `diff` promise a name's history; for a type that now keeps a row per package, a name's history is several items' histories, and a rollback by name could write one package's body into another's row. Refusing the unaddressed multi-slot read and the departed-holder rollback makes D3's refusal real on these doors; it does not take a declared capability away from a one-holder caller. The column is the right carrier (ruling A): a D4 customization's snapshot stays byte-identical and still names its row's package. Card Do 1 to 3 are met: rows carry the package, the three loader doors and the three manager doors take one, the pins iterate the live set, and both CONTROLs are present.

**must-fix:** none.

**should-fix**

- **S1 · the package-less row's versions have no address once a package also holds the name, and the changeset's remedy does not cover them.** `MetadataManager.register` of a package-less body on a name two packages hold writes the bare slot (`storeWriteKey`: holders ≠ 1 gives the identity), and `DatabaseLoader.save` stores it as a package-less row with a NULL-package history row. So "A, B and a package-less row" is a state first-party writers produce (it is R1b's own premise in #32347). The PR's note "no first-party writer produces such a row on a two-holder name after this change" does not hold against that code. After this PR the by-name read of such a name is refused with `{ kind: 'environment' }` among the candidates and the sentence "address it by its package", and no `packageId` selects that candidate; before, those versions were readable. The other D3 doors give the environment an exact qualifier (`not-held-by-qualifier` documents `callerPackageId: null` for it). The same gap shows as an inconsistency: `packageId: ''` or the `sys_metadata` sentinel is treated as a package by `historyPackageAddress` (reads match nothing and skip the several-slots refusal) but as the bare slot by `storeRowKey` in `rollbackSlot` (a direct `registerRollback` writes the package-less row). Close it one of two ways: give the address an explicit environment form judged by the store's own `isPackageCaller` rule on all three doors, with a pin; or keep the door as is, say in the changeset's "Who moves" paragraph that the package-less row's versions are unreadable while a package also holds the name, and file the follow-up card. Reach today is zero first-party callers, which is why this is not a must-fix.
- **S2 · `refuseSlotNotHeld` has two shapes that disagree with the sibling D3 door.** (a) A rollback naming a package when no row of the name is left (reachable through `MetadataManager.rollback` with a departed package's version) throws `not-held-by-qualifier` with `candidates: []`, and the sentence renders "it is held by . Address it by its holder." The exact-qualifier door answers its own miss when nothing holds the name, and the unnamed path here already throws the plain "not found for rollback". (b) A direct `registerRollback` naming A with a version of B while B still holds a row answers "not held by package B" with B among the candidates; through the manager this is masked by `getHistoryRecord` returning null first. Fix: no candidates falls through to "not found"; a version of another live holder is refused in words that say the version is that package's. Add a pin for (a).
- **S3** is in ②.

**nit**

- N1 · `queryHistory` by package reads every history row of the name, bodies included, and pages in memory. The ruling's reason for A was that "the driver filters and pages by the column"; the body-stamp fallback for legacy rows is why the code cannot. Correct, unbounded on a long history.
- N2 · the S8a guard cannot see a departed package's version that carries no attribution: a D4 customization saved before the column, or any row `SysMetadataRepository` wrote in a table both writers share. It still lands in the one remaining holder's row (the legacy pin asserts this as "as before"). The changeset's "cannot be restored into another package's row" is slightly wider than the code for those rows.
- N3 · tests: the options are passed `as never`, so the suite does not prove the widened parameter types it describes; the second S8a refusal (naming B) asserts `reason` only; no case pins a package beside the package-less row.
- N4 · the dev report says `check-adr-0087-registration` refused the changeset until its caller paragraph "lost its FROM/TO shape". The paragraph still tells a caller what to write. The disposition is right on substance (nothing stored converts), and the sibling changesets hold the same category, but it now rests on the detector not matching rather than on a category that fits a runtime-behaviour narrowing with a caller instruction. Worth one line to the gate's owner; not this PR's to fix.
- N5 · history records do not expose the package, so a one-holder caller reading by name cannot see which versions are a departed package's before the rollback refuses. `MetadataHistoryRecord` is a spec type and outside this card.
- N6 · candidate order in `refuseSlotNotHeld` is the rows' order; the exact-qualifier door lists packages, then the environment.

A should-fix is open, so this is not the final round: the fixes for S1 and S2 owe a delta review by this reviewer on the new head. A head that changes only the changeset (S3, or S1's second option) keeps this record.

Round: delta on record 6815918594 (PASS at `c2ad15cf6d1732a16da5092c30b6f2e194f83cc3`, should-fix S1, S2, S3). `c2ad15cf6..575073f3d` is two commits over five files (`database-loader.ts`, `metadata-manager.ts`, `package-slotted-store.ts`, `metadata-history.test.ts`, the changeset; +177 −61). The other 23 paths of the PR are byte-identical to the head that record reviewed.

Inputs read: record 6815918594, the PR body as re-patched, the delta diff, the three source files at the head around every changed door, the test diff, the head's check-runs, the file lists of #32507 #32513 #32558 #32548 #32533 #32551. Nothing was built or run. The dev's counts (81 passed, the two ablations, the md5 table, the `flow` probe) are the dev's readings and are not re-measured here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1: closed, with code and pin.** `MetadataHistoryAddress.packageId` is `string | null`. `addressedPackage` returns the package, `null` for `null` / `''` / `sys_metadata` (the store's `isPackageCaller`, the rule `storeRowKey` keys rows by), `undefined` for no address. `historyPackageAddress` (the two reads) and `rollbackSlot` both take their address from it, so the disagreement the last record named is gone. Reads compare `storedRowPackageId(row) ?? null`, so the environment address matches exactly the rows that name no package. Pin: the three-slot case reads versions, the record and a miss under each of `null`, `''`, `'sys_metadata'`; `diff` by `null`; a rollback by `''` that leaves both packages' rows equal; the refusal with no package-less row asserts `callerPackageId: null` and candidates [A, B]. The sentence renders "not held by the environment" (`packageScopedRefusalMessage` handles `null`).
- **S2a: closed.** `rollbackSlot` returns no slot when the name has no row, before any address is judged; `registerRollback` then throws its own "not found for rollback". Pin asserts the message and that `status` is undefined.
- **S2b: closed in words, not in envelope (N1).** A version attributed to another package that still holds a row throws a plain `Error` saying the version is that package's and which address restores it; `refuseSlotNotHeld` is reached only when that package holds no row. Pin asserts the message, no `refusal`, rows unchanged. Candidates in `refuseSlotNotHeld` are now packages first, then the environment (last round's N6).
- **S3: closed.** The changeset front matter names `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`.
- **`null` against "no option": no collision.** Every door tests `=== undefined` for "no address", so `null` is an address. On the head the three manager doors and the three loader doors have no caller outside `metadata-manager.ts` and tests (searched the whole tree), and `MetadataHistoryQueryOptionsSchema` in `packages/spec` carries no `packageId` key that a parser could default to `null`. No existing caller passes `null` to mean absent.
- **One holder, by reading: nothing moved in the delta.** With no address `addressedPackage` is `undefined` and each door takes the branch it took at `c2ad15cf6`. `rollbackSlot`'s early return on an empty name gives the unaddressed caller the same `{ rows: [] }` as before. The new "is package X's" branch needs X to hold a second row, which one holder never has. `historyAddressSuffix` and the registry write are unchanged when no address is given, and a type outside the set leaves every door at its first line.
